CURRENT USER MESSAGE: Why can a phone show its GPS position without mobile data, yet fail to show a detailed map?
ASSISTANT:

memory.scope: Sampled process peaks, not continuous maxima; includes profiling overhead. Fault counters are not physical-read counts.

answers.text: A phone can show its GPS position without mobile data because GPS relies on satellite signals to determine location. However, it may fail to show a detailed map when there is no signal from GPS satellites—such as in areas with poor coverage, dense urban environments, or during satellite outages—resulting in only a basic location pin or no map at all. Detailed maps require additional data, such as map services (e.g., Google Maps, Apple Maps), which are not available without mobile data or internet connectivity. Thus, while GPS can provide a location, detailed maps depend on external mapping data, which is typically accessed via mobile data or internet.
